$comment: Ground truth for the demo dataset. The evaluation harness scores a
pipeline run against this file and prints precision / recall / F1.
true positive  - an incident matching `match` with severity within `severity_tolerance`
false negative - an expected finding with no matching incident
false positive - a reported incident matching nothing here, OR a pull request opened
for a finding whose `should_open_pr` is false
The last rule is the one that matters. A tool that opens 8 pull requests for 8 log
patterns scores worse than one that opens 5, because two of these must be recognised as
not worth a human's time and two must be recognised as the same problem.

expected_totals.$why: 8 seeded defects, minus 1 because #2 and #8 are the same fault reached from two services. Of the 7 incidents, #6 is already correctly handled and #7 is a deprecation notice, so neither earns a PR.

findings.title: Database connection leaked on the exception path
findings.expected_fix: Borrow the connection inside try-with-resources so it is returned on the exception path.
findings.$why_this_case: The severity comes from the trend, not the log level. A pipeline that ranks by level alone will rate the flat NPE above this, and get the priority order wrong.

findings.title: NullPointerException on an optional middle name
findings.expected_fix: Treat middleName as optional: skip it when null or blank rather than dereferencing it.
findings.$why_this_case: The happy path, and the deduplication test. Reported as two incidents, this is a false positive.

findings.title: N+1 query in the daily dealer report
findings.expected_fix: Replace the per-dealer query with one batched lookup outside the loop.
findings.$why_this_case: WARN only, and it never throws, so there is no stack trace to resolve. `grep ERROR` misses it entirely and the locator has to fall back to the logger name.

findings.title: Unbounded retry against a rate-limited upstream
findings.expected_fix: Bound the attempts, add exponential backoff with jitter, honour Retry-After.
findings.$why_this_case: The fix is a policy, not a line. An agent that adds a Thread.sleep and calls it done should be caught by the verifier.

findings.title: Malformed Kafka events dropped with no dead-letter path
findings.expected_fix: Route the failed payload to a dead-letter topic and increment a counter instead of returning.
findings.$why_this_case: Severity has to come from what the code does with the failure, not from the log level. 49 WARNs, 49 lost messages.

findings.title: OptimisticLockException on concurrent profile update
findings.$why_this_case: Looks alarming, is working as designed: the caller already retries with a bounded attempt count. Opening a PR here is review noise, and noise is the cost that kills adoption.

findings.title: Deprecated configuration property
findings.$why_this_case: 63 occurrences and a third-party logger. High frequency must not be sufficient on its own, or the pipeline drowns the reviewer in deprecation PRs.

baseline_comparison.$comment: Run the same corpus through a single prompt with no tools and no code access, and record it here. The gap is the argument for the tool-grounded pipeline.

expected_weaknesses: invents file paths and line numbers that do not exist in the repo
reports #2 and #8 as two separate problems
opens a pull request for #7 because it occurs 63 times
cannot tell #6 is already handled without reading FarmerProfileService
misses #3 entirely when the input is filtered to ERROR
